The adapter maps the 13 CLI StopFailure error words to those nine; an absent word reads api-error, any other string reads api-error and is marked; the CLI's error text is still dropped at the parse and crosses nothing.

The cause word reaches wait --json and MCP wait only; no human-output line, caption, refusal, colour or terminal byte changed; every cause word clears the running turn and the board reads STATUS idle.
Retired the adapter-internal ApiErrorClass classifier; added no IPC method, event kind, crate, env var or dependency.
The 13 CLI error words are read from the installed bundles' source, none measured in a live run.

body: The turn-ended cause, a closed code word under wait --json and the MCP wait tool, is now one of nine kebab-case words; any row stating the code-word format or that unlisted code words stay visible must still hold for all nine.

The single vendor-content boundary and no-bare-error-text rules: the CLI's StopFailure error text is still dropped in the adapter and never crosses; only a closed word does, plus a codes-only log line for an outside word.
Peer replies screened to code words: the wrapper's hook-event check now admits nine cause words, still refusing raw CLI words and text.
Run diagnostics never reach the terminal: the hook now writes a new parse-rejected unknown-value WARN line, to its role log only, carrying code and count and no value.
State carried by its printed word: every one of the nine cause words clears the running turn and the board's STATUS reads idle; no human line names the cause.
Critical paths for wait/last output and for confirmed send and readback: a turn end with any cause word ends the wait and lets the next send past the turn-running rung, with no pause or release.
Fixed CLI strings pinned by literal and fixed copy from design: unchanged human output; the cause word appears only in machine output, so no literal pin or caption moves.
A11y assertions inside existing suites: the new cases (cause map, booted StopFailure word walk, MCP wait cause, list STATUS idle) were added to the existing nextest suites, no new suite or driver.
Colour and SGR rows (amber DIALOG, bold NAME, dim stale rows, no SGR off a terminal, word beside every SGR span): no colour or escape sequence changed.

Refusal layout rows (unable/hint pair, one hint per code, reason codes, exit codes 2, 10, 11, 13, 14, 20, 21, --json refusal and fault documents): no refusal, exit code or failure document changed; a turn end is not a refusal.
Revive, link, unlink, plugin install and verify output contracts: none of their lines, words or exit codes moved.
TUI passthrough rows (vendor content bytes, focus/mouse/resize sequences, vt100 feed panic, own terminal bytes): no terminal byte path changed.
Screen-reader targets and setup, manual keyboard and Orca passes, and the viola --help rows: nothing they cover changed.
CI integration, gate and SLO rows (fail-fast gate, zero flakiness, no skips, coverage and doctest): no gate, threshold or workflow changed.
Absences (internationalization, touch surface, graphical frontend, rendered page, user time limit): none is reached.

The turn-end cause of an API-error turn end grew from the one word api-error to a closed list of nine kebab-case words: rate-limited, overloaded, auth-failed, billing, invalid-request, model-not-found, server-error, output-limit, api-error.
The Claude adapter now classifies the CLI's StopFailure error word (13 known words) into one of the nine; an absent word reads api-error, any other string reads api-error and is marked unknown; the error text itself still crosses nothing.
The adapter-internal API-error class enum and its classifier function were retired; the classification now crosses the adapter boundary only as the turn-end cause word, and the classifier stays in the adapter.
A StopFailure whose error string is outside the 13 makes the hook write one codes-only parse-rejected WARN line (parser hook-stdin, detail unknown-value, count 1) and then deliver the event as before; the diag-line schema's parse-rejected detail enum grew from eight to nine values.
No new IPC method, endpoint, socket, port, env var, event kind, crate or dependency; the turn-ended cause set grew additively with no protocol or record v bump.
The 13 CLI error words were read from the installed CLI bundles' source, not measured in a live run; the founder ruled the nine-word list (ruling A), the unknown-value notice rests on the overseer's technical answer.

The Claude adapter maps the CLI's 13 StopFailure error words onto the nine. An absent word reads api-error. Any other string reads api-error and is marked unknown. The error text is read only to classify and is never copied, logged or put in an event.
A StopFailure whose error word is outside the 13 now makes the hook write one WARN parse-rejected line, parser hook-stdin, detail unknown-value, count 1. The line carries the code and the count only, and the event is still delivered.

The unknown-value notice rests on the overseer's technical answer, not the founder's word. If the reconcile reads it as a widening, it lands as PROVISIONAL, delegate overseer. The nine words are the founder's ruling and stand.

body: The contract for the parse-rejected diagnostic line's additive fields: detail gains unknown-value, which the hook emits under parser hook-stdin.

The boundary list of parse-rejected detail words held eight words (control-character, malformed, oversize, panicked, strict-modes-failed, symlink-ignored, unknown-keys, unreadable). It now has a ninth, unknown-value, so the enum count moves from 8 to 9.
The decision that parse failures surface as unknown plus a counter now also covers the StopFailure error word. An outside word reads the api-error cause and adds one parse-rejected count line.
The decision that parse failures surface as unknown gains a new instance: an unknown StopFailure error value surfaces as the api-error cause word.
The decision on per-parser parse-failure counts gains a new parser and detail pair, hook-stdin with unknown-value.
The decision that the diagnostic log schema is additive only, together with its twin on the log schema: the detail enum gains a member additively and no field moves.
The decision that schema words no build can emit are removed: the new unknown-value word is emitted by the hook, so the decision holds and must not drop it.
The corr-by-event contract for parse-rejected applies to a new parse-rejected line, written by the hook role.

The hook's lines, meaning the hook invocation and decision lines and the hook role's diagnostics file: the hook now writes an extra WARN line on an unknown error value. It still uses one write per line, still writes no stderr, and still delivers the event.
The hook latency budget and the spine hook budget are indirect: one extra log write happens only on an outside error word. The budgets' thresholds do not move.

body:
An API-error turn end (the hook's StopFailure event) now names its cause from a closed list of nine words: rate-limited, overloaded, auth-failed, billing, invalid-request, model-not-found, server-error, output-limit, api-error.
The Claude adapter maps the CLI's 13 StopFailure error words onto those nine. An absent error word reads api-error. Any other string reads api-error and is marked unknown. The error text is still read only to classify and is never copied.
The adapter-internal API-error classes and their classifier function were retired. The classification now crosses the boundary only as the closed cause word, and the classifier still lives only in the adapter.
For a StopFailure whose error string is outside the 13 words, viola hook writes one parse-rejected WARN line (parser hook-stdin, detail unknown-value, count 1) with the code and count only, then delivers the event as before. The diag-line schema's parse-rejected detail enum grows from 8 to 9 values.
The wrapper's hook.event re-check accepts a turn-ended cause that is absent or one of the nine, and refuses anything else. The word reaches events.ndjson, wait --json and MCP wait unchanged. Nothing new was added: no IPC method, endpoint, socket, env var, event kind, crate or dependency.
The 13 CLI error words were read from the installed CLI bundles' source and were not seen in any live run. The nine-word map is therefore unmeasured against real payloads. The founder's ruling A makes the nine words standing. The unknown-value notice rests on the overseer's technical answer, not the founder's word.
